pages.text:
Vilmorin-Andrieux et Cie, Les plantes potagères: description et culture des
principaux légumes des climats tempérés. Paris, 1891.

Source Gallica / Bibliothèque nationale de France
https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k8630130c
BnF, département Sciences et techniques, shelfmark 8-S-6938
Rights Public domain (published 1891). Gallica conditions of use:
https://gallica.bnf.fr/html/und/conditions-dutilisation-des-contenus-de-gallica
Accessed 2026-08-30

THIS IS A PARTIAL ACQUISITION -- READ BEFORE USE
------------------------------------------------
Gallica returns an HTML interstitial instead of a PDF to non-browser clients,
and rate-limits its IIIF image endpoint (HTTP 429 after five rapid requests).
Rather than hammer it, the tomato pages were identified with Gallica's
ContentSearch API and only those were fetched, at full resolution, with a 20 s
base delay and exponential backoff.

HELD (18 page images, tomate_chapter_pages/, named f<document-page>.jpg):
f0012 - passage on North American breeding ("et surtout tomates")
f0656 - f0672 - the TOMATE chapter, printed pp. ~632-644
NOT HELD:
the rest of the 764-page volume, including 'tomate' mentions that
ContentSearch located on document pages 31, 112, 500, 680, 724, 736, 742,
745, 752, 754 and 755.

Page images are IIIF native JPEGs, ~2560x4240 px, ~0.9-1.4 MB each. The
variety woodcuts are captioned "Fruits de grosseur naturelle" -- life size --
so they are scale-bearing and can be scored directly.

Key passages (printed page numbers):
p.633 TOMATE ROUGE GROSSE: "très gros, déprimés, irrégulièrement côtelés,
larges de 0m,07 à 0m,10, épais de 0m,04 à 0m,05" + the note that
tomato canning is "une industrie très développée" in the Midi.
p.636 TOMATE ROUGE GROSSE LISSE (= ANGL. "Trophy tomato"): "difficile à
conserver absolument pure; les fruits tendent toujours à redevenir
côtelés."
p.636 TOMATE CHAMPION: "très lisses, bien faits et passablement déprimés",
"rouge violacé et non franchement écarlate".

To complete the volume, re-run scratchpad gallica.py with the remaining page
numbers, or fetch it from a browser session.
